device.description: Quad 12-bit voltage-output DAC with 16-bit serial input, double-buffered (LOADREG, LOADDACS) and reset to zero or mid scale
device.note: dac7715.pdf (SBAS140) p.2-3 electrical characteristics (VCC 14.25-15.75 V, VIH 3.325 V, VIL 1.575 V, straight binary), p.4 absolute maximum (digital inputs -0.3 to 5.8 V), p.5 pin configuration and descriptions, p.12-14 digital interface, Figure 4 timing, Table I timing, Table II control logic, Table III serial shift register

commands.note: Figure 4: A1 A0, two unused bits, D11-D0 MSB first, shifted on CLK rising while CS is low (CS and CLK are OR-ed)

pages: p.2-4 (electrical, logic levels, abs max), p.5 (pinout), p.12-14 (digital interface, Figure 4, Tables I-III)
notModeled: analog: outputs, VREFH/VREFL reference inputs, single (+15 V) or dual (+-15 V) supply operation

logic thresholds are fixed (VIH 3.325 V, VIL 1.575 V; digital inputs -0.3 to 5.8 V abs max) and there is no logic supply pin: vcc is the VCC +15 V range, so the voltage check cannot flag a digital input above 5.8 V

LOADREG (pin 14) transfers the shift register into the input register A1 A0 select (transparent while low); the model writes the input register when the 16th bit is clocked in, as if LOADREG were pulsed after each word
LOADDACS: all DAC registers transparent while low (modeled as LDAC level active low)

CS and CLK are OR-ed and interchangeable (either can clock the shift register); a CS rise with CLK low shifts one extra bit; the shift register keeps the last 16 bits clocked, the model decodes the first 16 bits after CS falls
power-on state is not specified; registers reset to 0
variants: DAC7715U / DAC7715UB are linearity grades of one chip; DAC7714 (no LOADREG, pin 13 NIC) and DAC7715 (LOADREG on pin 14, LOADDACS on pin 13) have their own datasheets
